      "body": "DD-R CERTIFICATE LANE \u2014 DURABLE FINDINGS (run 0048 r1, 2026-07-25). Supersedes I-0327.\n\n1. chart-avoid is ANSWERED: NO. The Z(diamond) chart does not confine its divisors. Do not\n   re-open it, and do not re-attempt the \"theta side\" of spec-dd-r ADDENDUM 2 \u00a74: Theta =\n   fiberWeilDivisor pi is supported on V_0 \\ V_1, so set-theoretically Theta = V_1^c and the\n   \"tractable half\" is a WHOLE DISJUNCT of the verdict; and IsGenerator.dvd makes supportLocus\n   the base locus of K, so the hypothesised exact-pole generator exists iff the conclusion\n   already holds. Circular.\n\n2. THE COUNTEREXAMPLE IS FIELD-INDEPENDENT. F = s X_0^2 + X_0 X_1 + s X_1^2 over k[s] cuts an\n   irreducible degree-2 relative Cartier divisor whose fibre at s = 0 is {0, infinity}, and it\n   stays irreducible over every nonempty open of the base. s(x^2+1) + x is degree 1 in s with\n   coprime coefficients over ANY field, so this works over F_2. Consequence: \"assume k infinite\"\n   is NOT an escape from the obstruction, and small finite fields are a genuine hole in every\n   avoidance-based repair. (The example was already in the tree as a docstring model at\n   Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:170-175.)\n\n3. THE OBSTRUCTION NEEDS NO CONNECTIVITY. isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_isCertified\n   (Picard/DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean, landed this round): a certificate forces BOTH pinned\n   chart traces closed, full stop. Use this form, not the preconnected one, when refuting.\n   And it is DivEq-invariant (DivEq.supportLocus_eq, same file), so it bites the DivFamZar\n   QUOTIENT \u2014 re-spelling the equations is not an escape either.\n\n4. TWO CONSTRAINTS, NOT ONE. (c1)-finiteness = leak-freeness gives per-piece swallow-or-miss for\n   ANY cover by opens, so a connected support lies inside a single PIECE no matter how\n   FinCoverData is reshaped. Only the chart-wise partitions of unity (DivisorFamily.lean:174,176)\n   upgrade that to a single CHART. Sharp form: no repair keeping pieces inside the preimages of\n   a FIXED PAIR of points of P^1 can work. UNTRIED CHEAP OPTION: relax the partitions to a joint\n   \u2a06 pieces = top \u2014 drops the requirement from two avoided points to one.\n\n5. DEAD END, with a reason: deleting clause (c1) from IsCertified. Module.Flat R (colength j) is\n   free from fibrewise regularity alone (flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField,\n   SupportTube.lean:313 \u2014 no finiteness, no no-leak), so it looks like finiteness is the only\n   culprit. It is not usable: every (c2)/(c3)/(c4) keystone in SlicingFlatKernel.lean (variable\n   block :221-224) carries [Module.Finite R M] with M = chartProd, which IS finite colengths.\n\n6. pi-GENERICITY IS TOTAL, and DivScheme is pi-FREE. The only constraints on pi anywhere are\n   [IsFinite pi], [IsDominant pi], [IsAffineHom pi] and the propositional triangle hpi; DivScheme\n   (DivScheme.lean:144) takes two abstract CurveDivisors and pi enters only at the instantiation.\n   So a coordinate twist needs no atlas gluing. But Aut(P^1) does not exist in this project, and\n   mathlib has Proj.map without Proj.mapIso; and the project has no k-rational points of P^1 at\n   all.",

The claim lives only in `informal/spec-dd-r.md`. So there is no blueprint statement to contradict \u2014 and also no mathematical specification of what `divRep` is meant to represent.\n\nThe one fact `I-0337` listed as missing (its fact 6, \"(c1) forces leak-freeness is proved nowhere\") is closed: `supportLeak_eq_empty_iff_finite_colength`, `Picard/DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean`, commit `5651710d6`."

      "body": "DOCSTRING BULLETS IN THIS TREE ARE NOT EVIDENCE THAT A DECLARATION EXISTS.\n\nEstablished 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 2) by two independent adversarial audits, and it is\nthe single highest-value generalizable lesson from four rounds of recon on AJCR.\n\nThe pattern: a module docstring lists \"Main declarations\" that the file never declares; a\nroadmap row then quotes the docstring; a lane is then briefed on the roadmap and burns a\nsession looking for a sorry that is not there.  Confirmed instances:\n  * `PicEtAff.degAff_mapAlg` and `mem_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_iff` -- the roadmap called them\n    cheap items with a \"verbatim template\"; they are NOT sorries to close, they do not\n    exist as declarations anywhere.\n  * `PicRepColimitCompat.lean:54-56` -- an English-only \"hence\" standing in for a proof.\n  * `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean` and `Pic0ChartLocusOpen.lean` both discussed\n    `chartLocus` in prose for months; it had ZERO code hits until 2026-07-26.\n  * `Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean:41-48` -- the header asserts the file \"elaborates green\"; the\n    file has no olean, ilean, trace or hash, so nothing in it has ever been checked.\n\nRULE: before briefing a lane, or writing a roadmap row, or quoting a \"cheap item\", run\n  /home/axel/.archon-env/bin/horizon search \"<name>\" --json\nand require a hit with a signature.  One second per claim.  Apply this to your own\ndocstrings too: do not announce a theorem you have not declared.",

      "body": "NOTE APPENDED 2026-07-26 (run 0048 round 2): item 3's \"cheaper option\" is REFUTED; the\nhuman question in this item STANDS and is still yours.\n\nREFUTED: \"relaxing just the chart-wise partitions to a joint covering drops the requirement\nfrom two avoided points to ONE.  Worth trying before anyone builds PGL_2.\"  It buys nothing,\nand the reason is a typing fact, not a failed proof.  FinCoverData types its pieces INTO the\ncharts -- `h0 : Fin m0 -> Gamma(relCurve, V0)` (DivisorFamily.lean:166), `h1` into V1 (:168),\n`pieces := Sum.elim (basicOpen . h0) (basicOpen . h1)` (:186) -- so every piece is a basic\nopen of one of the two PINNED charts by construction, whatever the partition data says.\nPer-piece swallow-or-miss already holds for any cover by opens (DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98\nuses only openness), so a connected divisor still lands in one piece, and `basicOpen_le` puts\nthat piece inside one chart.  Changing the partition FIELDS cannot change where the pieces\nLIVE.  Recorded as roadmap leaf ...ddr.certificate.joint-cover, status rejected, with the\n10-file rebuild cost if anyone tries it anyway.\n\nThe sharp form to quote from now on: NO repair that keeps the pieces inside the preimages of\na FIXED PAIR of points of P^1 can work.  Only R1 (vary the pinned pair -- needs Aut(P^1)) or\nR2 (generalize the piece type) remain.\n\nSTILL OPEN AND STILL YOURS: over a small finite field, where |P^1(k)| = q + 1 < n + 2, what\nis DivFamZar supposed to be?  Nothing in the three options below has changed.\n\n--- ORIGINAL ---\nCORRECTION TO MY ANSWER ON I-0333, filed in the same round after an adversarial pass. The\nNEGATIVE half of that answer stands unchanged: chart-avoid is NO, decisively, and you do not\nhave to take that decision. The POSITIVE half \u2014 \"the repair is cheap and it is not a decision\" \u2014\nwas too optimistic in three ways, and one of them puts a DIFFERENT question back to you.\n\nWHAT SURVIVED. The Z(diamond) chart does not confine its divisors; the counterexample is real;\nthe obstruction is DivEq-invariant and therefore bites DivFamZar itself; confinement is an open\ncondition on the base, so an atlas may legitimately record avoidance. All kernel-checked or\nargued in informal/spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 3.\n\nWHAT DID NOT.\n 1. The counterexample is FIELD-INDEPENDENT (irreducibility of s(x^2+1)+x needs nothing of k),\n    so it also kills the \"assume k infinite\" escape I proposed. Enlarging the field does not\n    help.\n 2. The repair RELOCATES the forbidden geometric input rather than removing it: fibrewise-finite\n    support is not implied by anything a LocalEquations carries, and must be discharged from the\n    seed's own degree data.\n 3. My diagnosis \"the binding constraint is FinCoverData\" was too narrow. Per-piece\n    swallow-or-miss follows from (c1)-finiteness for ANY cover by opens; only the chart-wise\n    partitions of unity upgrade \"inside one piece\" to \"inside one chart\". Sharp form: no repair\n    keeping pieces inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR of points of P^1 can work. A cheaper\n    option I had missed: relaxing just the chart-wise partitions to a joint covering drops the\n    requirement from two avoided points to ONE. Worth trying before anyone builds PGL_2.\n\nTHE QUESTION THAT IS NOW YOURS, and it is a different one from I-0333's:\n\n  OVER A SMALL FINITE FIELD, WHERE |P^1(k)| = q + 1 < n + 2, WHAT IS DivFamZar SUPPOSED TO BE?\n\nCertifiability needs two k-rational points of P^1 off the support's image at every base point.\nChallenge.lean:96-99 states the Jacobian over an ARBITRARY field, and nothing in Picard/ or\nRiemannRoch/ assumes more than [Field k]. Three options, not comparable on mathematical grounds\nalone:\n (a) accept |P^1(k)| >= n + 2 as a hypothesis and record that the challenge as stated is then\n     not solved for small q;\n (b) plan a descent lane \u2014 divQProj (Picard/DivSchemeQProj.lean) is the right lever for fpqc\n     descent from a big enough k'/k;\n (c) generalize the pinned charts to closed points of degree d >= 2, paying\n     Gamma(P1 k, chartOpen k i) iso Polynomial k (Curve/P1Charts.lean:234,239) and\n     isPrincipalIdealRing_chartSections (Curve/P1Points.lean:64), since Cl(P^1 minus a degree-d\n     point) = Z/d.\n\nRoadmap leaf: AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.field-size (blocked, high). It should be\nsettled BEFORE anyone builds the GL_2(k) action on P^1 (leaf p1-aut) \u2014 it decides whether that\nwork is worth doing at all.",

      "body": "THE divRep GATE IS MIS-STATED IN THREE WAYS. I-0234 is archived because it\n   was DONE.  Nobody is waiting on a rebuild window.  Delete that clause from both places.\n\n2) U1's SUBSTRATE IS FAR MORE COMPLETE THAN THE ROW SAYS, AND U1 IS NOT CERTIFICATE-FREE.\n   The row says only \"`divUniversalFamily` greps empty\".  True, but:\n     * seedUniv : ThetaGeneratorSeed over R_Z EXISTS -- Picard/DivSchemeSeedUnivGen.lean:283.\n     * The fibrewise keystone EXISTS and is proved --\n       existsUnique_effective_divisor_divUniversalFibre (DivSchemeSeedUnivAssembleKappa.lean:417)\n       and its residue-field spelling (:481): at every prime of the pair chart ring over the\n       carve ideal, a UNIQUE effective degree-g divisor cuts both universal windows.\n   So U1 = seedUniv + IsGenerator + ThetaGeneratorSeed.certifiedFamily\n   (Picard/DivSchemeEps.lean:234), and `certifiedFamily` demands\n   `(D.divisorAdaptation hD).IsCertified g` -- a GLOBAL certificate over R_Z.\n   CONSEQUENCE: ddr.divrep is NOT an independent mountain from ddr.certificate.  The roadmap's\n   \"SIX INDEPENDENT MOUNTAINS\" framing hides that U1 sits directly on the certificate gate the\n   chart-avoid no-go closed.  Fix the master summary.\n   NOTE ALSO that this refutes I-0320's headline \"NO CONSUMER EVER NEEDED [IsCertified over R]\":\n   divRepPullAt (Picard/DivRepAffKit.lean:92) takes\n   `U i j : CertifiedDivisorFamily C (ChartRing i j) pi g`, a global certificate at R_Z.\n\n3) CHEAP EDIT NOBODY HAS MADE: divRepPullAt's `U` can be weakened from CertifiedDivisorFamily\n   to DivFamZar.  Its body is `DivFamZar.mapAlgHom omega (DivFam.mk (U i j)).toZar` -- it only\n   ever uses the toZar image.  Retyping `U : forall i j, DivFamZar C (ChartRing i j) pi g` and\n   `divRepPullAt ... := DivFamZar.mapAlgHom omega (U i j)` is strictly weaker, keeps\n   divRepPullAt_id/_comp and IsCompatible verbatim, and is what makes I-0320's relaxation\n   actually reach U1 (the pointwise gate\n   isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation then applies at R_Z, so the\n   adaptation need not be the opaque `.some`).\n\n4) I-0350's #1 RANKED MOVE, `pull_naturality`, IS ILL-POSED.       "body": "THE CHART-AVOID COUNTEREXAMPLE IS OFF-STRATUM.  Ground review, 2026-07-26.\n\nThe structural no-go is sound and I am not disputing it: (c1)-finiteness IS leak-freeness\n(DivSchemeCertZarC1.lean), piece traces are clopen in the support (DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98),\nFinCoverData types its pieces into the two pinned charts (DivisorFamily.lean:166,:168,:186), and\nthe obstruction is DivEq-invariant (DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean).  Those are degree-agnostic.\n\nWHAT IS OVERSTATED is the \"explicit counterexample\" that roadmap leaf chart-avoid (c),\nAJCR.w4-rep's master summary, and informal/spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 3 all lean on:\n  F = t X^2 + X Y + t Y^2 over k[t], with C = P^1 and pi = id.\nThat divisor has DEGREE 2 on a curve of GENUS 0.  The campaign's functor is\ndivFunctor C pi g / DivFamZar C S pi g with g pinned to the genus by the standing hypothesis\nhchi : Sheaf.chi = 1 - g (DivRepClassifyZarSep.lean:147, DivRepAffKit.lean:62), and\nIsCertified n's clause (c2) fixes the glued colength's fibre rank to n, i.e. n = deg D\n(DivisorFamily.lean:426-437).  So the witness lives in divFunctor P^1 id 2, NOT in\ndivFunctor P^1 id 0, which is the functor the campaign must represent for that curve.\n\nWHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING PEDANTRY.  On the campaign's own stratum:\n * g = 0: degree-0 relative divisors have empty support and the no-go is vacuous.\n * g = 1: degree 1, i.e. a section.  A section CAN meet both pinned fibres over a connected\n   base (t |-> [t : t-1] hits 0 at t=0 and infinity at t=1), but its support locus is\n   Spec R, so removing one of the two base points confines it -- and the certificate gate is\n   pointwise on the base after the I-0320 relaxation.  So base shrink DOES evade the no-go at\n   g = 1.  Irreducibility over every shrink, which is what makes the exhibited example\n   shrink-stable, needs degree >= 2.\n * g >= 2 is where the no-go actually bites, and no witness has been exhibited there.\n\nACTION (cheap, and it should be done before p1-aut or R2 is costed): produce a genus->=2\nwitness, or state plainly in ADDENDUM 3 and the roadmap that the counterexample is exhibited\noff-stratum and that the on-stratum claim rests on the degree-agnostic structural argument\nalone.       "body": "ANSWER TO I-0333 ITEM 1 (run 0048 round 1). The design decision you were asked to take is no\nlonger needed: the question is settled by mathematics, and the lane is now blocked on ordinary\nwork rather than on you. Deliverable of record: informal/spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 3; Lean:\nPicard/DivSchemeCertZarConfine.lean (6 declarations, 0 sorries, axioms exactly\n[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], in the default build).\n\nTHE ANSWER IS (b), AND SHARPER THAN (b). The Z(diamond) chart does NOT confine its divisors:\n\n * the seed carries no exactness datum, and every universal instantiation of its `side` field\n   picks an ARBITRARY chart containing the point, so a point of pi^-1(infinity) is legal;\n * option (a) was never available: Theta = fiberWeilDivisor pi is supported on V_0 \\ V_1, so\n   set-theoretically Theta = V_1^c and the \"theta side\" of ADDENDUM 2 \u00a74 is one WHOLE disjunct\n   of the verdict, not a tractable half of it \u2014 and its argument is circular;\n * there is an explicit counterexample: over k[t], F = t X^2 + X Y + t Y^2 cuts an IRREDUCIBLE\n   relative Cartier divisor of degree 2 whose fibre at t = 0 is {0, infinity}, and which stays\n   irreducible over every nonempty open of the base. No Zariski shrink separates the witnesses.\n   (The witness the lane had been citing for this, Spec R[x]/(x^2-t), never meets\n   pi^-1(infinity) and is chart-confined \u2014 it does not exhibit the phenomenon.)\n * and the obstruction is DivEq-invariant (landed this round), so it bites the DivFamZar\n   QUOTIENT, not merely a chosen representative. DivFamZar is not the relative-divisor functor.\n\nWHY YOU DO NOT HAVE TO CHOOSE. The two branches you were offered are not alternatives: the\ncarve IS the redesign, and it is legitimate for a reason that is now a theorem. The binding\nconstraint is FinCoverData (pieces are basic opens of the two PINNED charts, with a partition of\nunity on each) \u2014 not pi, not the cover's fineness, not the submodule L, not the base. So a\nrepair must introduce a piece not inside a single pinned chart, and the cheapest such repair is\nto let the atlas vary the P^1-coordinate (pi becomes gamma . pi). That is FREE in every landed\ndeclaration, because the whole chain is generic in pi. Its one missing input is Aut(P^1), which\nthis project does not have (P1 k is a Proj; no PGL_2 action anywhere) \u2014 a self-contained piece\nof ordinary mathematics, now roadmap leaf ...certificate.p1-aut.\n\nAnd the carve does not lose points: chart confinement is an OPEN condition on the base\n(isOpen_setOf_fibre_subset_chartInter, landed), and confinement at one fibre spreads to a\nZariski neighbourhood. That is exactly what distinguishes an atlas RECORDING avoidance from a\nprover ASSUMING it, which \u00a7Discipline (2) rightly forbids.\n\nWHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS NOT A DECISION: p1-aut (the GL_2(k) action on P^1) -> fibre-avoid (every\nrelative divisor avoids two k-points of P^1 Zariski-locally on the base) -> cert-relocalize\n(restate IsLocallyCertified/DivFamZar to quantify over the twist) -> swallow-adapt ->\ncert-collapse -> cert-assemble. Two hypotheses need YOUR eye, but later and separately:\n (i) the avoidance argument wants k INFINITE, while Challenge.lean states the Jacobian over an\n     arbitrary field. A finite-field route needs |P^1(k)| > deg D \u2014 a base change to k(T) or a\n     degree-d point. Flagging now so it is scheduled, not discovered late.\n (ii) DivRepGlobalData's `equiv` field asserts a full equivalence for a FIXED pi and therefore\n     cannot hold as stated; cert-relocalize must re-pin it.\n\nITEM 2 OF I-0333 (the harness problem) is untouched by this and still stands.",

      "body": "THE Z-CLOPEN CERTIFICATE PRINCIPLE (DD-1/DD-2 lanes, 2026-07-17 \u2014 three independent sightings in one day; treat as a standing design constraint for every DAT-D brick).\n\nA DivisorAdaptation piece carries an R-finite-projective colength \u2014 clause (c1) of IsCertified \u2014 IFF the piece's trace on the divisor scheme Z = V(D) (finite flat over Spec R) is CLOPEN in Z.       "body": "THE DD-R CERTIFICATE'S NO-LEAK CLAUSE IS A CHART-DESIGN CONDITION, NOT A FIBRE CONDITION\n(proved in Lean 2026-07-25, run 0048, commits 49866bdd1 + 206967379; standing constraint for the\ncertificate lane).\n\nTHE THEOREM. A FinCoverData carries a partition of unity on EACH pinned chart, so the chart-b pieces\ncover all of V_b and the union of their traces is the whole chart trace supportLocus cap V_b. A\nfinite union of closed sets is closed, hence\n\n  the assembler's hnoLeak at every piece  ==>  supportLocus cap V_0 and supportLocus cap V_1 are\n  CLOSED in the relative curve.\n\n`DivisorAdaptation.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak`\n(Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean). The conclusion mentions neither the adaptation nor its\npieces \u2014 only the system and the two pinned charts.\n\nFOUR CONSEQUENCES, all binding:\n1. REFINING THE COVER CANNOT HELP. The union of the piece traces is the fixed set supportLocus cap\n   V_b; a finer cover only imposes MORE closed-trace constraints on the same union. So roadmap leaf\n   leak-image route (b) (\"refine the adaptation near a bad prime\") is DEAD, and so is any\n   support-tube / packet-idempotent scheme aimed at producing hnoLeak piece by piece.\n2. SHRINKING THE BASE CANNOT HELP EITHER, except by restating the same condition over the smaller\n   base. The pointwise gate's freedom is real but it buys a different thing (see 4).\n3. THE OBLIGATION IS: the chart's divisors avoid both vertical fibres of pi, i.e.\n   supportLocus subset V_0 cap V_1. It is FALSE for a general degree-g divisor \u2014 model:\n   V(t x^2 + x y + t y^2) in P^1 over k[t] has a DOMAIN section ring (no nontrivial idempotent after\n   any base shrink) and fibre {0, infinity} at t = 0, so no adaptation of it can ever be certified.\n   The DD-R atlas must arrange the avoidance. Roadmap leaf ...certificate.chart-avoid.\n4. THE POSITIVE SHAPE IS \"SWALLOW OR MISS\": if every piece either contains the whole support or\n   misses it, hnoLeak and clause (c1) follow with no fibre analysis, and a missing piece has a UNIT\n   equation so its colength VANISHES (Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean). The pointwise gate\n   `isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` accepts ANY adaptation over the\n   shrunken base \u2014 so CONSTRUCT this one instead of certifying\n   `(exists_divisorAdaptation ...).some`.\n\nRULE: before proving a clause of `IsCertified`, ask which adaptation you are proving it FOR. Seven\nsessions were spent proving clauses for `ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation`\n(= `.some`, DivSchemeFamily.lean:367), about which nothing is known.       "body": "GROUND (run 0048 r0 checkpoint) \u2014 three defects in the run-0048 certificate-lane slice; all cheap to fix, one is a dangling reference to a file that does not exist.\n\n(1) DANGLING REFERENCE + UNPROVED SUFFICIENCY CLAIM.\nAlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean:33-35 claims:\n  \"supportLocus \u2229 V\u2080 and supportLocus \u2229 V\u2081 closed is not merely necessary, it is *sufficient*,\n   because the two-piece adaptation whose pieces are the pinned charts themselves realizes it\n   (`DivSchemeCertZarChartPair.lean`).\"\nThat file DOES NOT EXIST (find/grep over the whole workspace: the string occurs only in this docstring). That is not free; it is essentially the content of swallow-adapt step (b). Either delete the sentence or state the missing hypothesis.\n\n(2) THE NEW CHAIN chart-avoid -> swallow-adapt IS UNDER-SPECIFIED AND WILL NOT COMPOSE AS WRITTEN.\nchart-avoid is titled \"is the DD-R chart s divisor confined to ONE pinned chart?\" and states its goal as\n  supportLocus \u2286 V\u2080 (or the V\u2081 twin).\nswallow-adapt consumes forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint, whose hypothesis is swallow-or-miss at EVERY piece.       "body": "The idempotent brick cannot be applied to a colength module directly: colength ideals are generated by NONZERODIVISORS, never by 1-e\n\nRecorded 2026-07-25 after reviewing run 0047 s0014. Module.{Projective,Flat}.quotient_span_singleton_one_sub_of_isIdempotentElem (Picard/DivSchemeCertZarLeak.lean:79,106) are correct: mult-by-e is a well-defined R-linear section of B -> B/(1-e) because e*((1-e)*c) = 0, and the retraction identity mkQ (e*b) = mkQ b holds since e*b - b = (-b)*(1-e). Both discharged via Projective.of_split / Flat.of_retract.\n\nBut note the arithmetic before planning the packet route: A.colength j = Gamma(pieces j) / span {A.eqn j}, and A.eqn j is a NONZERODIVISOR (derived, DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular; primitive field LocalEquations.regular, DivisorClass.lean:120). If span {f} = span {1 - e} with f a nonzerodivisor and e idempotent, then e = 0 and the ideal is the WHOLE ring, so the quotient is the zero module. Verified in Lean as a standalone example: e*f = 0 from f = (1-e)*d, then f*e = 0 plus f in nonZeroDivisors forces e = 0.\n\nConsequence: the brick can never be applied with B = a piece section ring and the cut ideal being the colength ideal. It only applies at one level up - to the packet algebra Gamma(Z) = W(d) or a piece's trace algebra, where the cutting ideal is genuinely idempotent-generated. Any future session that tries to feed A.colength j into the brick will get the zero module and a vacuous certificate. The roadmap comment C-0002 on leak-image already flags the OTHER trap in the same chain (step (ii): getting the idempotents from W(d)'s own clause (c2) is circular).",

      "body": "SUPPORT-SEPARATED ADAPTATIONS CANNOT CERTIFY A GENERAL DD-R SYSTEM (proved in Lean 2026-07-25, run 0047).\n\nTHE TEMPTING ROUTE. The pointwise gate (isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation,\nDivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean:162) accepts ANY adaptation over the shrunken base. So one is tempted\nto choose an adaptation that is SUPPORT-SEPARATED (off-diagonal ovlColength i j all subsingleton).\nThat really does trivialize the hard part: the Cech difference deltaLeft - deltaRight becomes LITERALLY\nZERO, the equalizer W(d) is the whole product, and both flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) plus the\nkernel-spanning hypothesis are free. Landed as DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_separated\n(Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean), needing only (c1) + a rankAtStalk sum.\n\nWHY IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE LANE. The premise is essentially always FALSE. Proved as\nDivisorAdaptation.supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated (same file): BOTH pinned charts carry\na partition of unity (FinCoverData.partition0/1, DivisorFamily.lean:174-176), so their pieces cover V0\nand V1 respectively (cover0/cover1, DivisorFamily.lean:199-207). A support point z in V0 cap V1\ntherefore lies in a chart-0 piece AND a chart-1 piece \u2014 an off-diagonal pair \u2014 and both equations have\nnon-unit germ at z (isUnit_germ_eqn_iff, SupportTube.lean:245), so that overlap ideal is PROPER and its\ncolength is not subsingleton. Hence separation holds only if supp d avoids V0 cap V1, i.e. the divisor\nis confined to the two vertical fibres of pi. Refining the cover cannot help; the pointwise gate cannot\nhelp either (shrinking the base deletes fibres, it does not move a support point out of the overlap);\nand supportLocus is DivEq-invariant, so re-spelling d cannot help.\n\nALREADY KNOWN FOR THE FIELD CASE. DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:33-38 records the same obstruction in\nprose and routes around it: over a field every module is free, so the certificate is discharged on the\nPLAIN extraction adaptation via the unconditional CRT colength-degree identity\n(DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_deg, DivisorFamilyFieldSurj.lean:104; deg_presentationDivisor,\nDivisorFamilyFieldCRT.lean:365, I-0230). That escape is unavailable over a nonreduced base, which is\nexactly why the flat-cokernel content stands.\n\nRULE. Do not attack the DD-R certificate by choosing a cleverer adaptation. Two independent no-gos now\nbound the packaging: cleverer submodule L is ruled out by divUniversalHighWindowKernelSyzygySpans_iff_flat_quotient\n(DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean:298, spanning IFF the sought flatness), and cleverer PIECES are ruled out\nby supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated. The honest analogue of the field escape is a RELATIVE\nversion of the stalk-CRT adaptation-independence of the glued rank, not separation. See [[I-0209]], [[I-0320]].",

      "body": "Recipe: building ModuleCat-R morphisms into sheaf-of-modules section objects (v4.31) \u2014 the ConcreteCategory.ofHom + presheaf-obj pattern, and the let-fvar IsIso gotcha\n\nLanded in `tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen` (`QuotScheme.lean`, T12 run 0010). When you need `f : ModuleCat.of R M \u27f6 <sections object>` (e.g. to feed `tilde.map`):\n\n- **Target the honest `ModuleCat R` object** `(modulesSpecToSheaf.obj G).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op \u22a4)` \u2014 this is literally the domain module of Mathlib's `fromTilde\u0393`/`toOpen`. Do NOT target `moduleSpec\u0393Functor.obj G` via `ModuleCat.ofHom`/`\u2192\u2097` type ascriptions: elaboration whnf-unfolds the carrier past `restrictScalars`, and `Module R <unfolded carrier>` synthesis then fails (no refold; a letI at the folded form does not match either).\n- **Construct via `ConcreteCategory.ofHom { toFun := ..., map_add' := ..., map_smul' := ... }`** with the expected hom type ascribed \u2014 the instances come from the objects via the `(\u00b7 \u2192\u2097[R] \u00b7)` FC family, no synthesis. A bare `let blin : M \u2192\u2097[R] <object> := ...` fails; skipping the standalone LinearMap and going straight to the categorical hom works.\n- **map_smul' across compHom-vs-restrictScalars actions**: `change` the goal to the native-action form `(\u0393SpecIso R).inv.hom r \u2022 f x`, then `rw [\u2190 hact]; exact h1` where `hact : appLE V \u22a4 e = (\u0393SpecIso R).inv` (proved by `rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE, fromSpec_app_self, Category.assoc, \u2190 Functor.map_comp, \u2190 op_comp, Subsingleton.elim _ (\ud835\udfd9 \u22a4), op_id, map_id, comp_id]`).\n- **IsIso of `tilde.map b'` for a `let`-bound b'**: `haveI : IsIso (tilde.map b') := by rw [show tilde.map b' = (tilde.functor _).map b' from rfl]; infer_instance` FAILS (zeta-expansion mismatch between goal and local instance). Use `inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((tilde.functor _).map b'))` \u2014 works even without `clear_value`.\n- **Unit-component bijectivity at open immersions**: `Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (restrictAdjunction j) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction j) N` + `restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app` (plain presheaf restriction along `j''\u1d41j\u207b\u00b9\u1d41V = V`) + component of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`. When `rw [\u2190 AddCommGrpCat.comp_apply]` fails with \"target not type-correct under instances transparency\" (`\u0393((\ud835\udfed X.Modules).obj N, V)` forms), do `change`-restatement at the type-correct form, then close with `exact congrArg (fun \u03c6 => (AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom \u03c6) y) hcomp` where `hcomp : f \u226b g = \ud835\udfd9 _` \u2014 both sides defeq, no rewriting in the wall.\n- **\u03a3-pair trace**: `tilde.toOpen_map_app` (naturality) + `toOpen_fromTilde\u0393_app` at `\u22a4` (+ `homOfLE le_top = \ud835\udfd9 \u22a4` by `Subsingleton.elim`) give `(tilde.map b' \u226b fromTilde\u0393).app \u22a4 \u2218 toOpen = b'` elementwise, via `congrArg`-chains only.",

      "body": "**Recipes: module-level d\u00e9vissage in Lean v4.31 (landed in FlatteningStratification GenericFreeness, run 0010 T12 r2) \u2014 reuse for any prime-filtration/SES argument.**\n\n- **ModuleCat SES arguments need ONE universe**: `ModuleCat.ofHom {X Y : Type v}` forces all modules of a `ShortComplex (ModuleCat R)` into the same universe. Binders `{M\u2081 M\u2082 M\u2083 : Type*}` give distinct universes and produce baffling failures \u2014 instance goals displayed as raw `Quot \u21d1(OreLocalization.oreEqv ...)` (LocalizedModule unfolded past its instance heads) plus universe-mismatched `Eq.{max u_1 u_4}` vs `Eq.{max u_1 u_2}`. Pin `Type v`. The d\u00e9vissage eliminator is single-universe anyway.\n- **`set S := Submonoid.powers (f*g)` breaks instance unification** in localized-module types (same family as the known let-fvar IsIso gotcha): instance search will not zeta-unfold the set-fvar when unifying `Localization S'` heads. Write the submonoid term explicitly everywhere; `let`-bound MAPS (data) are fine \u2014 only types/instances mind.\n- **Quantified-instance motive** for `IsNoetherianRing.induction_on_isQuotientEquivQuotientPrime` when the property lives over a DIFFERENT ring A than the induction ring B: `motive N _ iMB _ := \u2200 (iA : Module A N), @IsScalarTower A B N Algebra.toSMul iMB.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSMul iA.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSMul \u2192 @P A N _ _ iA`. Cases: subsingleton via @-application; quotient case transports along `(e.restrictScalars A).symm` (canonical tower on B\u29f8p is instance-found); exact case builds `letI iA\u2081 := Module.compHom N\u2081 (algebraMap A B)` + tower `\u27e8fun a b n => by change (a \u2022 b) \u2022 n = algebraMap A B a \u2022 b \u2022 n; rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_smul]\u27e9`; B-linear maps restrict via `LinearMap.restrictScalars A` and inj/surj/Exact transfer definitionally. Final application `... \u2039Module A M\u203a \u2039IsScalarTower A B M\u203a` unifies. Compiled essentially first-try.\n- **Two-localization freeness transport** (`M_f` free \u27f9 `M_{fg}` free) WITHOUT IsLocalizedModule-composition: `(IsLocalization.Away.awayToAwayRight f g).toAlgebra` + `IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (awayToAwayRight_eq ..).symm`, then equiv-chain `congr(refl, isBaseChange f) .symm \u226a\u226b cancelBaseChange \u226a\u226b isBaseChange (f*g)` and `Module.Free.tensor` + `Module.Free.of_equiv'`. Give every LinearEquiv a fully-typed `have` \u2014 `refine LinearEquiv.trans ?_ e` with open source type sticks on RingHomCompTriple metavariables.\n- **Localized SES**: `IsLocalizedModule.map/map_injective/map_surjective/map_exact` at `mkLinearMap`s, upgrade R-linear\u2192Loc-linear with `LinearMap.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization` (coe unchanged, so Function.Exact/Injective/Surjective transfer by defeq); `ShortComplex.mk (ofHom u') (ofHom v') (ModuleCat.hom_ext (LinearMap.ext fun x => hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero x))`; ShortExact via `moduleCat_exact_iff` + `mono_iff_injective` + `epi_iff_surjective`; finish `ModuleCat.free_shortExact`.\n- **refine-under-binder**: `refine subsingleton_of_forall_eq 0 fun x => ?_` fails (?_ under lambda); use `apply` + `intro` + `induction x using LocalizedModule.induction_on with | _ m s => ...`. `Submonoid.mk_smul` bridges `(\u27e8c,hc\u27e9 : \u21a5S) \u2022 m` to `c \u2022 m`.",

      "body": "**tangentSpaceIso (A.3.iii) is NOT directly provable \u2014 critical path runs through the relative Pic functor, and a naive FGA rewire is a FALSE-axiom trap.**\n\n- `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso` (`Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`) cannot be proven against the current foundation: `picSharp` in `FGAPicRepresentability.lean` is `Classical.choice` of a `\u27e8sorry\u27e9` `Nonempty` \u2014 a fully opaque functor. Any rewire must use the relative (and in general sheafified) functor.\n- Proof-pattern notes: the `Quotient.lift`/`Quotient.sound` + iso-chain style (pullbackCongr/pullbackId/pullbackComp `.app`, D4\u2032 `pullbackTensorIsoOfLocallyTrivial`, `pullback_pullback_eq`) compiled essentially first-try \u2014 no v4.31 transparency walls in this corner. `pullback.lift_fst/snd` are NOT simp (only `@[reassoc]`); pass them + their `_assoc` forms to `simp` explicitly after `pullback.hom_ext`.",

  \[
    \check H^1_{\mathrm{ff}}(D)\times\Omega_K(D)\longrightarrow k.
  \]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
  A functional in \(\Omega_K(D)\) factors uniquely through the
  finite-dimensional quotient

  functional on that quotient pulls back to such a Weil differential.
  This gives the first isomorphism; transport it across

\end{proof}

\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}

\end{proof}

algebra structure on `K(C)`, every nonzero constant `c ∈ k` has order `0` at
every prime divisor: `c` is a unit in the field `k`, hence its image in each

Audit verdict (see module docstring): TRUE at this generality — no properness,

scoped instance instIsConstantField (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    [IsIntegral C.left] [IsLocallyNoetherian C.left]
    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne C.left] :
    Adelic.IsConstantField k C.left where
  order_algebraMap_eq_zero P c hc := by
    letI : Algebra ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point) :=
      C.left.presheaf.algebra_section_stalk
        (⟨P.point, trivial⟩ : (⊤ : C.left.Opens))
    haveI : IsScalarTower ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point)
        C.left.functionField :=

    have h1 : algebraMap k C.left.functionField c

    have hu : IsUnit (algebraMap ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤) (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point)

    rw [h1, IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply ↥Γ(C.left, ⊤)
      (C.left.presheaf.stalk P.point) C.left.functionField]
    exact Scheme.RationalMap.order_algebraMap_eq_zero_of_isUnit P hu

\section{Weil differentials and duality}
\label{sec:RiemannRoch_Adelic_duality}

The adelic evaluation pairing identifies the dual of the twist cokernel
with a space of Weil differentials.  A fixed nonzero differential then
turns this space into an ordinary Riemann--Roch space.

\begin{proposition}[The principal-parts resolution]
  \label{thm:adelic_principal_parts_resolution}
  \notready
  \uses{def:adelic_divisorial_sheaf, def:adelic_orderGe}
  Let \(\mathcal K\) be the sheaf of rational functions and let
  \[
    \mathcal P_D=
      \bigoplus_P i_{P,*}
        \bigl(K/\mathfrak G_P^{\ge-D(P)}\bigr).
  \]
  There is an exact sequence
  \[
    0\longrightarrow\struct C(D)\longrightarrow\mathcal K
      \longrightarrow\mathcal P_D\longrightarrow0,
  \]
  in which \(\mathcal K\) and \(\mathcal P_D\) are flasque, and
  \(\Gamma(C,\mathcal P_D)\simeq
    \mathbb A_K/\mathbb A_K(D)\).
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
  Exactness is stalkwise.  At the generic point the first arrow is the
  identity of \(K\).  At a closed point \(P\), its kernel is the
  fractional ideal \(\mathfrak G_P^{\ge-D(P)}\), and the quotient is the
  displayed principal-parts module.  The rational-function sheaf is
  constant on nonempty opens of the integral curve and is flasque; each
  skyscraper summand is flasque, and a finite-support section of their
  direct sum extends componentwise.  Finally an adele modulo
  \(\mathbb A_K(D)\) records exactly its finitely many nonzero principal
  parts, which gives the global-section isomorphism.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Adelic and two-chart cohomology agree]
  \label{thm:adelic_adele_cover_compare}
  \notready
  \uses{thm:adelic_principal_parts_resolution,
    thm:adelic_function_field_H1_compare}
  For every divisor \(D\),
  \[
    H^1_{\mathbb A}(D)
      =\mathbb A_K/(\mathbb A_K(D)+K)
      \simeq_k\check H^1_{\mathrm{ff}}(D).
  \]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
  Taking global sections of
  \Cref{thm:adelic_principal_parts_resolution} identifies its degree-one
  cohomology with the cokernel of
  \(K\to\mathbb A_K/\mathbb A_K(D)\), namely
  \(\mathbb A_K/(\mathbb A_K(D)+K)\).  Thus this quotient is
  \(H^1(C,\struct C(D))\), which is the two-chart quotient by
  \Cref{thm:adelic_function_field_H1_compare}.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Weil differentials]
  \label{def:adelic_weil_differentials}
  \uses{thm:adelic_adele_cover_compare}
  \source{papaioannou-algebraic-rr:page-0011}
  A Weil differential is a \(k\)-linear form on \(\mathbb A_K\) that
  vanishes on \(\mathbb A_K(E)+K\) for some divisor \(E\).  Write
  \(\Omega_K\) for their union and
  \[
    \Omega_K(D)=
      \{\eta\in\Omega_K:\eta(\mathbb A_K(D)+K)=0\}.
  \]
  Multiplication by \(x\in K\) is defined by
  \((x\eta)(\alpha)=\eta(x\alpha)\), making \(\Omega_K\) a
  \(K\)-vector space.
\end{definition}

    \check H^1_{\mathrm{ff}}(D)\times\Omega_K(D)\longrightarrow k.

\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Eventual vanishing of the adelic index]
  \label{thm:adelic_index_eventually_zero}
  \notready
  \uses{thm:adelic_module_finite_genus,
    thm:adelic_adele_cover_compare,
    thm:adelic_riemann_inequality,
    thm:adelic_principal_degree_zero}
  There is an integer \(c\) such that
  \(H^1_{\mathbb A}(D)=0\) whenever \(\deg D\ge c\).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  Choose adele representatives of a basis of the finite-dimensional space
  \(H^1_{\mathbb A}(0)\).  Every representative belongs to
  \(\mathbb A_K(B_j)\) for some effective divisor \(B_j\); a common upper
  bound \(B\) therefore kills the basis under the surjection
  \(H^1_{\mathbb A}(0)\to H^1_{\mathbb A}(B)\), so the latter space is zero.
  Put \(c=\deg B+g\).  If \(\deg D\ge c\), the Riemann inequality gives
  \(\ell(D-B)>0\).  For nonzero \(f\in L(D-B)\), the divisor
  \(E=D+\operatorname{div}(f)\) satisfies \(E\ge B\), hence
  \(H^1_{\mathbb A}(E)=0\).  Multiplication by \(f^{-1}\) identifies the
  quotients for \(D\) and \(E\), proving the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The divisor of a Weil differential]
  \label{thm:adelic_weil_differential_divisor}
  \notready
  \uses{def:adelic_weil_differentials,
    thm:adelic_residuePairing,
    thm:adelic_index_eventually_zero}
  \source{papaioannou-algebraic-rr:page-0012}
  For every nonzero \(\eta\in\Omega_K\) there is a unique divisor
  \(\operatorname{div}(\eta)\) maximal among the divisors \(D\) for which
  \(\eta\in\Omega_K(D)\).  Consequently
  \[
    \Omega_K(D)=\{0\}\cup
      \{\eta\ne0:\operatorname{div}(\eta)\ge D\}.
  \]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  The set \(M(\eta)=\{D:\eta\in\Omega_K(D)\}\) is nonempty by the
  definition of a Weil differential.  If \(D\in M(\eta)\), then \(\eta\)
  gives a nonzero functional on \(H^1_{\mathbb A}(D)\); hence
  \Cref{thm:adelic_index_eventually_zero} bounds the degrees occurring in
  \(M(\eta)\).  Choose \(W\in M(\eta)\) of maximal degree.  If
  \(D_0\in M(\eta)\) and \(D_0(Q)>W(Q)\), decompose any
  \(\alpha\in\mathbb A_K(W+Q)\) into the adele supported away from \(Q\)
  and the adele supported at \(Q\).  The first lies in \(\mathbb A_K(W)\)
  and the second in \(\mathbb A_K(D_0)\), so \(\eta(\alpha)=0\).  Thus
  \(W+Q\in M(\eta)\), contradicting maximality.  Therefore every
  \(D\in M(\eta)\) satisfies \(D\le W\), which proves existence,
  uniqueness, and the displayed characterization.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Scaling a differential]
  \label{thm:adelic_weil_differential_divisor_mul}
  \notready
  \uses{thm:adelic_weil_differential_divisor}
  \source{papaioannou-algebraic-rr:page-0012}
  For \(x\in K^\times\) and \(0\ne\eta\in\Omega_K\),
  \[
    \operatorname{div}(x\eta)
      =\operatorname{div}(x)+\operatorname{div}(\eta).
  \]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  Multiplication by \(x\) carries \(\mathbb A_K(E)\) isomorphically onto
  \(\mathbb A_K(E-\operatorname{div}(x))\).  Hence
  \(x\eta\in\Omega_K(E)\) exactly when
  \(\eta\in\Omega_K(E-\operatorname{div}(x))\).  Comparing the unique
  maximal divisors on the two sides gives the formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[One-dimensionality of Weil differentials]
  \label{thm:adelic_weil_differentials_finrank_one}
  \notready
  \uses{thm:adelic_residuePairing,
    thm:adelic_weil_differential_divisor,
    thm:adelic_weil_differential_divisor_mul,
    thm:adelic_riemann_inequality,

    thm:adelic_chi_eq_chi_zero_add_degree}
  \source{papaioannou-algebraic-rr:page-0011,
    papaioannou-algebraic-rr:page-0012}
  The \(K\)-vector space \(\Omega_K\) is one-dimensional.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  First \(\Omega_K\ne0\): for \(\deg D\ll0\), the identity
  \(i(D)=\ell(D)-\deg D-1+g\) makes \(i(D)>0\), so
  \(\Omega_K(D)\simeq H^1_{\mathbb A}(D)^*\) is nonzero.  Choose
  \(0\ne\eta_i\in\Omega_K(D_i)\) for \(i=1,2\).  For an effective
  divisor \(B\) of sufficiently large degree, multiplication gives
  injections
  \[
    L(D_i+B)\hookrightarrow\Omega_K(-B),\qquad x\longmapsto x\eta_i.
  \]
  The Riemann inequality bounds the two source dimensions below by
  \(\deg(D_i+B)+1-g\), while negative-degree vanishing and the
  \(\chi\)-identity give
  \(\dim_k\Omega_K(-B)=i(-B)=\deg B+g-1\).  For \(\deg B\) large, the
  two images therefore have positive-dimensional intersection.  Thus
  \(x_1\eta_1=x_2\eta_2\ne0\) for some \(x_i\in K^\times\), and
  \(\eta_2=(x_1/x_2)\eta_1\).  Every two nonzero differentials are
  proportional.
\end{proof}

  \label{thm:adelic_serreDuality}

  \source{papaioannou-algebraic-rr:page-0011,

  For a canonical divisor \(K_C = \operatorname{div}\omega\) of a nonzero
  Weil differential \(\omega\), the map \(x \mapsto x\omega\) induces a
  \(k\)-linear isomorphism
  \[
    \mu \colon L(K_C - D) \;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\; \Omega_K(D)
      \;\simeq_k\; H^1_{\mathbb A}(D)^*
      \;\simeq_k\;\check H^1_{\mathrm{ff}}(D)^*,
  \]
  so that \(i(D)=\dim_k\check H^1_{\mathrm{ff}}(D)=\ell(K_C-D)\).
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
  By \Cref{thm:adelic_weil_differentials_finrank_one}, every Weil
  differential is uniquely \(x\omega\).  By
  \Cref{thm:adelic_weil_differential_divisor_mul},
  \(\operatorname{div}(x\omega)=\operatorname{div}(x)+K_C\); hence
  \[
    x\omega\in\Omega_K(D)
      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
    \operatorname{div}(x)+K_C\ge D
      \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in L(K_C-D).
  \]
  This proves the first isomorphism.  The second is
  \Cref{thm:adelic_residuePairing}, and the third is
  \Cref{thm:adelic_adele_cover_compare}; taking dimensions gives the final
  equality.
\end{proof}
